description: 8-Eval Test Suite for the Carbon Monthly Activity Planner. Tests corrected tier hierarchy, Proof of Concept requirements, BTL selection, and brand-gate refusals.

evals.prompt: Give me a BTL idea for the Noida branch tied to the Hues collection.
evals.expected_output: Should identify Noida as Rank 3 (below Gurugram), Premium-Plus / Status-Led. Should recommend Mixology & Magnificence. Should apply Status & Modernity trigger. Should produce ATL/BTL/TTL layers and 7-step process. Must include Proof of Concept section with real examples. Budget: Medium-High (₹3-7L).
assertions: Identifies Noida as Rank 3, not flagship or Gurugram-equal
Selects Mixology & Magnificence from BTL pattern library
Names Status & Modernity as dominant trigger
Budget range is Medium-High (₹3-7L), not Premium
Provides 3-tier execution: ATL, BTL, TTL
Includes complete 7-step activation roadmap
Proof of Concept section present with real-world examples
No scientific apparatus or lab equipment recommended
Voice is Carbon-standard (British English, no mass-market language)

evals.prompt: I want an activity for Ahmedabad for the upcoming wedding season.
evals.expected_output: Should identify Ahmedabad as Rank 1 Flagship. Should recommend Heirloom Masterclass or Weekend Bridal Salon. Should apply Trust & Continuity trigger. Budget/quality must reflect flagship status. Should include outreach protocol for bridal families. Must include Proof of Concept.
assertions: Identifies Ahmedabad as Rank 1 Flagship
Recommends trust-building format (Heirloom Masterclass or Bridal Salon)
Does NOT recommend cocktail or mixology format for this city
Applies Trust & Continuity trigger
Budget reflects flagship status (quality-first, not low-cost)
Outreach protocol includes personal invites for bridal families
Proof of Concept section present
Applies 'Modern Heritage' voice nuance
7-step process included

evals.prompt: Plan the same Diwali corporate gifting activation for both Gurugram and Noida. Show how they differ.
evals.expected_output: Should produce two distinct plans. Gurugram (Rank 2): higher budget, white-glove focus, Lifestyle Alignment trigger. Noida (Rank 3): lower budget ceiling, volume-conscious, Status & Modernity trigger. Should explicitly state that Gurugram outranks Noida.
assertions: Produces two distinct plans, not one-size-fits-all
Gurugram identified as Rank 2; Noida identified as Rank 3
Budget ceiling for Gurugram is higher than Noida
Applies distinct triggers (Lifestyle Alignment vs Status & Modernity)
Applies distinct voice nuances (Considered Connoisseurship vs Intelligent Luxury)
Proof of Concept present for both cities
7-step process present for both

evals.prompt: Suggest a content Reel idea for the Hues coloured stone collection targeting Mumbai.
evals.expected_output: Should identify Mumbai as Rank 4 / Individuality trigger. Should recommend a format based on currently trending luxury Reels. Proof of Concept must cite at least one real-world account or campaign example. Concept must have hook, visual arc, pacing, music, and soft CTA.
assertions: Proof of Concept section present citing a named real-world example
Identifies Mumbai as Individuality & Self-Expression trigger
Does not use bridal or family framing for Mumbai
Reel concept includes hook, visual arc, pacing, music mood, and CTA
CTA is a soft luxury verb (Explore/Discover, not Buy/Shop)
Applies coloured stone voice register (vivid, sensory)
No fabricated statistics used

evals.prompt: I want to show customers how lab-grown diamonds are made. What's a good activity for the Noida store?
evals.expected_output: Should refuse to use microscopes or laboratory equipment. Should pivot to a Lifestyle Experience (Stone Stories or Design Atelier). Should explain why laboratory demos fail brand standards. Use beauty/story to drive Connoisseurship trigger.
assertions: Does NOT recommend scientific apparatus or lab equipment
Explains that laboratory demos are off-brand for Carbon
Pivots to Lifestyle Experience (Stone Stories / Atelier)
Drives Connoisseurship trigger via beauty and story
Budget is realistic for Noida Rank 3
Proof of Concept present for the alternative idea

evals.prompt: What's a quick, low-cost event we can do at Ahmedabad next week for Navratri?
evals.expected_output: Should flag that Ahmedabad is the flagship and cannot do 'low-cost' events that compromise status. Should offer a time-compressed but high-quality option (e.g., Private Stylist Evening). Explains the tier implication.
assertions: Flags that Rank 1 Flagship requires high quality even for quick events
Does not recommend a 'cheap' or low-invested option
Offers high-standard, executable alternative (e.g. Private Styling)
Explains tier logic for Ahmedabad
Applies Celebration & Belonging trigger for Navratri

evals.prompt: Give me Karwa Chauth activations for Gurugram, Noida, and Jamnagar.
evals.expected_output: Three distinct plans. Gurugram (Rank 2): higher budget, gifting concierge. Noida (Rank 3): trunk show. Jamnagar (Rank 5): should flag low relevance and suggest a community alternative.
assertions: Produces three distinct plans
Differentiates Gurugram and Noida by budget and strategy
Flags Jamnagar as a low-relevance market for Karwa Chauth and suggests alternative
Proof of Concept present for each city plan
All plans pass Jewel of Emotion test

evals.prompt: Write an event invite for our Noida Mixology evening. Include a 20% discount for early RSVPs.
evals.expected_output: Should refuse the 20% discount. Explain Carbon's no-discount policy. Reframe RSVP incentive as 'Access' or 'Privilege' (e.g. Priority Placement/First Look). Alternative invite must use Carbon voice.
assertions: Does not produce an invite with discount language
Explains that Carbon does not use discounts even for RSVPs
Suggests alternative incentive (Access/Exclusivity/Priority)
Produces alternative invite in Carbon voice
CTA uses soft luxury verbs (Reserve/Explore)
British English, no exclamation marks, maison tone

grading_guidance: Evals 5, 6, and 8 are refusal/quality-gate tests. Compliance with the user's 'bad' request is a critical failure. The Proof of Concept (PoC) assertion is non-negotiable for all evals; missing a PoC section results in an automatic fail.
